findings.text: follow-on: the head graph arm's header declares revision=2066467588a80f4a9c0df302ccc23714a3b62fe8 while the arm measured the reworked module committed at 33981d6e5; the in-log probe printing _ATTACHMENTS_QUERY.format(scope="") can only succeed on the reworked template, whose sole placeholder is {scope}, so the declared revision is one commit behind the module the 9 failed / 22 passed figure describes and a reader comparing revisions cannot tie the evidence to the code the probe proves was imported.

follow-on: the new read restates the invariant's producer predicate (live_producer.status <> 'stale') rather than composing it from its owner imas_codex/standard_names/source_invariant.py:42, so the hold can drift from find_sourceless_live_names if that predicate gains another excluded status. The derived-parent half is composed (attachment_audit.py:179 wraps _derived_parent_cypher), so only the producer half is duplicated; composing it would have needed a helper in source_invariant.py, outside this node's write scope.

follow-on: the hold's exemption set is populated only from the derived-parent clause (sn_stranding_exempt), omitting the status='superseded' half of the invariant's retired_is_exempt clause (source_invariant.py:53-56), so a name with status='superseded' and a non-superseded name_stage would be held and reported as an operator worklist item where require_producing_sources would release it, diverging from the brief's 'superseded names ... exempt exactly as the invariant exempts them'. Latent rather than reachable: every writer that sets status='superseded' sets name_stage='superseded' in the same statement (graph_ops.py:23038, graph_ops.py:23751, signed_manifest.py:4878, signed_manifest.py:5457).
